summary: Canonical MCP output bounding (SPEC v2) on the mirror (shell-out) path: Etsy-owned bound.Mirror core with opaque v2 cursors, 16 MiB stdout capture, one-level agent descent, per-response byte budget, cursor registration for literal read-only + local mirror tools, inline --rules-json/--control-ids with an OS-aware pre-exec argument guard, explicit market --compact projection, and an env-driven (PP_MCP_MAX_BYTES, default 32000) budget for the whole bound package.
reason: The generated mirror captured only a preview-sized prefix and returned non-resumable bound.Text previews cut mid-JSON, PP_MCP_MAX_BYTES was ignored, market gaps/price could not run over MCP (file sinks hidden, stdin not fed) and --compact was a no-op for market commands. The machine has not adopted the canonical contract (#3090), so the pager lives in an Etsy-owned file with narrow, marked edits at generated call sites.
reprint_status: Verified by a dry-run (no --apply) of cli-printing-press 4.35.6 regen-merge against a fresh tree generated from spec.json with the same version (the fresh bound.go, shellout.go, typemap.go, walker.go are byte-identical to the pre-change generated files, so the fresh tree is a faithful base). Verdicts: internal/mcp/bound/bound.go TEMPLATED-CLEAN (a future --apply would OVERWRITE it, reverting `var MaxBytes = Budget()` to `const MaxBytes = 60000`; the classifier does not see the const-to-var change); internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go TEMPLATED-WITH-ADDITIONS and internal/mcp/cobratree/typemap.go TEMPLATED-WITH-ADDITIONS (left untouched, edits preserved); internal/mcp/cobratree/walker.go and internal/mcp/tools.go TEMPLATED-CLEAN (not edited by this patch); internal/mcp/bound/etsy_canonical.go, mkt_helpers.go, mkt_rules.go and all new tests NOVEL (kept); market_demand.go, market_gaps.go, market_price.go TEMPLATED-WITH-ADDITIONS (kept); internal/cli/which.go TEMPLATED-CLEAN (identical because the fresh tree was generated with the updated research.json); bound_test.go TEMPLATED-VALUE-DRIFT (the two budget-relative fixtures, flagged for manual merge). No redeclared MaxBytes can occur (etsy_canonical.go never declares it), so the fallback shape (var budgetBytes) was not needed. Simulated outcome of the only lossy verdict: copying the fresh bound.go over the committed tree builds, but `go vet ./internal/mcp/bound` fails loudly because etsy_canonical_test.go assigns MaxBytes in refreshBudgetForTest (cannot assign to a const), so a lost MaxBytes edit cannot pass the gate silently.
reapply: After a reprint or regen-merge --apply (bound.go is the only file the classifier would overwrite; shellout.go and typemap.go are kept as TEMPLATED-WITH-ADDITIONS, but verify each item): (1) internal/mcp/bound/bound.go: replace the const `MaxBytes = 60000` line with `var MaxBytes = Budget()` placed before the const group (keep MaxItems, maxPreviewBytes in the group). (2) internal/mcp/bound/bound_test.go: restore the two budget-relative fixtures (TestJSONReturnsCompactFullArrayWhenIndentedOutputExceedsBudget, TestEndpointLocalPageResponseKeepsFittingHistoricalList). (3) internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go must still carry: `const shelloutCaptureLimit = 64 << 10` (a fixed stderr cap with no budget coupling) and newCappedCapture growing on demand; the 16 MiB stdoutCapture with StdoutBytes/StdoutOverflow on CLICommandResult; toolResultFromCLICommandFor calling bound.Mirror with the per-call Budget and Reserve; secondaryText and hintsDroppedMarker on the success, failure and help paths; bound.TextWithin(s, budget, reserve) for both single-block and two-block failures; the cursor strip gated on cursorEligible(cmd) (falling back to allowedStructuredArgs["cursor"] only when the command is unknown), then checkMirrorArgLimits and bound.DecodeMirrorCursor before RunCLICommand; mirrorOptions sourcing SupportsCursor from cursorEligible(cmd) when the command is known, SnapshotParam from allowed["snapshot"], the MCP-spelled Narrow list (top, limit, select, compact, pages, per-page) and the generic NoRerun text; and guardMirroredMCPCall stashing the command in the context. (4) internal/mcp/cobratree/typemap.go must still carry cursorEligible (literal mcp:read-only, pp:data-source local, no native cursor flag, money summary excluded by command-path suffix) with both the schema property and the allowed-argument registration behind it; walker.go, helpers.go and cliArgsFromMCP stay untouched. (5) Keep the Etsy-owned files: internal/mcp/bound/etsy_canonical.go, the three etsy_testmain_test.go files (they unset PP_MCP_MAX_BYTES and re-derive bound.MaxBytes), the Etsy test files, mkt_helpers.go projection, mkt_rules.go inline helpers and caps, the market gaps/price inline flags and help text. (6) Regenerate which.go/README/SKILL from research.json so the byte-identical drift tests pass. (7) Run `go build ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l internal)"` and the hermetic suite (`env -u ETSY_API_KEY -u ETSY_SHARED_SECRET -u ETSY_SHOP_ID PATH="/bin:/usr/bin:$PATH" go test -count=1 ./...`), also once with PP_MCP_MAX_BYTES=4000 exported. A missing edit fails loudly in TestMCPOutputNeverExceedsBudget, TestEtsyMCPBoundingSeam, TestEtsyPerResponseBudget, TestMirrorArgGuardBeforeExec, TestMarketCompact, TestHardeningBudget and the bound package compile (etsy_canonical_test.go assigns MaxBytes).
deviations: Spec D0 ("never a hand-editable generated file") is not met for the edited call sites (bound.go MaxBytes, shellout.go, typemap.go, bound_test.go fixtures, sink-conformance test); unavoidable until the machine adopts the contract (#3090). walker.go and helpers.go are untouched.

Under budget with no cursor, mirror stdout passes through byte-identical to the CLI (spec section 5 says not to pass an under-budget non-envelope blob through raw). Documented rule: when top-level `truncated` is absent the output is complete. A call that supplies a cursor always returns an envelope, including the final page.

Typed, code-orchestration, search and sql paths keep their generated shapes, v1 cursors, the 50-item fit cap, linear fit loops, `_pp_truncated`/`resumable` previews, no oversized* fields and two resume-parameter names (`_pp_cursor`, `cursor`); only their byte budget changes (60000 -> 32000, env-overridable). Binary-response ceiling drops from about 45 KB to about 24 KB. Deferred to #3090.

Mirror Preview shape is {truncated,oversized:false,max_bytes,original_bytes,preview,note}; `preview` is a string fragment, never JSON; `_pp_truncated`/`resumable` are not emitted on the mirror path. WithMetadata (keys on _pp_truncated) is unchanged and unreachable from the mirror path (registeredPlatformSource is nil).
Spec D2 `limit` parameter is not registered; the market tools' own --top/--limit/--select/--compact/--snapshot serve as narrowing and are named in the over-budget note.

Cursor registration is split across shellout.go (strip + pre-exec decode, because the handler must see the cursor) and typemap.go (schema property and allowed argument behind one shared predicate, cursorEligible = literal mcp:read-only annotation + pp:data-source local + no native cursor flag). The v3 plan's alternative of adding cursor to the CLI-blocked set was not used. walker.go stays untouched, so the handler learns SupportsCursor from allowedStructuredArgs["cursor"] and the registered command from a context value set by guardMirroredMCPCall.

cursor is registered (inertly) on tags and trend: their over-budget output is a Preview (array-free or scalar arrays), which never pages. money_summary is cursor-eligible but emits since/until from the current wall-clock second, so a cursor on an over-budget money_summary result fails safe with cursor_stale; its determinism-table row tolerates only those two fields.
Mirror cursors are v2 (`{k:"m",v:2,t,a,o,d}`) so the typed decodeEndpointCursor (v1 only) rejects them. Check order: length cap (1024) -> decode -> k/v -> t -> a before exec; d -> o after exec.

Step 6 reserves a short marker for the stderr-hints block before sizing the primary block, so the reported max_bytes is the full budget while the primary block is smaller by the marker length whenever hints exist.
Single-block failure results use bound.TextWithin(first, budget, 0), the same mirror Preview shape as two-block failures (round 2 D5; supersedes the round-1 bound.Text note).

The real registered tree has seven non-local literal read-only mirrors (analytics, learnings_candidates, learnings_list, learnings_stats, playbook_list, recall, workflow_status); all reject cursor before any child spawns. None is annotated data-source auto.

Inline caps are 96 KiB (98304 bytes) for --rules-json and --control-ids; the MCP pre-exec guard is 120 KiB per argument on non-Windows and 31 KiB of escaped command line (plus a fixed 260-byte executable allowance) on Windows, replacing the v2 24 KiB/30 KiB text. Inline control ids are validated as positive decimal integers; file --control keeps its permissive parsing.

D-K compact: an explicit --compact (or MCP compact:true) projects market demand/shops/price/gaps/tags rows to fixed key sets and replaces the generic compaction (copied flags with compact=false); --agent's implied compact does not trigger it and --select wins. Trend and snapshot are unchanged.

Live MCP smoke (step 2, behaviour only): 5 Etsy calls into an isolated store; market_demand paged to completion at PP_MCP_MAX_BYTES=4000 over the real stdio MCP server with the union equal to the CLI output. Hermetic seam tests cover the same paths without quota.

Mutation proofs: 22 mutants plus the typed-guard mutant, each CAUGHT with its knock-out and control (see mcp-canonical-bounding-proof.md); one first attempt for the bound.Text-revert mutant was refused (knock-out scope unproven because a seam row aborts the parent test) and was re-run against a non-aborting row.

Five cursor-registered tools never page because their result is a single object: market_tags, market_trend, money_reconcile, reviews_digest and shop_attention; over budget they return a non-pageable Preview. The registry has 15 cursor tools: 5 snapshot tools, 5 single-object tools and 5 other list tools (10 tools register no snapshot param).
docs: research.json is the source for the market gaps/price why_it_matters text; which.go, README.md and SKILL.md carry the same strings byte-for-byte (TestMarketDocsWhichDrift plus the inline-flag docs test). README.md and SKILL.md gained a 'Paging MCP results' section; CHANGELOG.md gained an Unreleased section with the old-to-new mirror shape table, the typed budget change and the new flags and guard.
